gold: Over the years, first-year chemistry has come to be taught in a more routinely methodical fashion, which dampens its intellectual appeal.

state: In the Life of reflection, Nozick wrote: I will not, like Socrates, say that life without reflection is not worth living-it is too harsh. But if our life is guided by thoughtful reflection, then it is the life we live for ourselves, not someone else's. In this sense, life without reflection is an incomplete life.
instructions: Which of the followings cannot be derived from Nozick's statement?
options: Nozick thinks that a life worth living is a life of self-reflection
Nozick believes that only a life that lives for oneself is a complete life
Nozick believes that a complete life is a life of reflection
Nozick believes that life without reflection is not a complete life
gold: Nozick believes that only a life that lives for oneself is a complete life

state: The researchers mixed a certain plant lactic acid bacteria into the feed of the experimental rats. After the experimental rats ate the feed for 4 weeks, they continued to exert mental pressure sufficient to cause sleep disorders for two weeks, and then let the experimental rats pedal the wheel during the nocturnal activity period to test their activity. The results showed that the downward trend of the activity of the experimental rats extracted with the lactic acid bacteria was curbed, However, the rats in the control group who did not eat the feed containing the lactic acid bacteria had difficulty falling asleep during the day and lack of sleep, resulting in a significant decrease in their activity at night. Therefore, the researchers believe that the intake of lactic acid bacteria can improve the sleep disorder caused by mental stress.
instructions: Which of the followings, if true, questions the above conclusion most?
options: The experimental rats usually sleep during the day and come out at night
The expression of a gene related to sleep disorder was inhibited in the experimental mice extracted with lactic acid bacteria
The composition of the plant lactic acid bacteria is inconsistent with that of most lactic acid bacteria
In addition to pedaling the wheel, the experimental rats had no other activities at night
gold: The composition of the plant lactic acid bacteria is inconsistent with that of most lactic acid bacteria

state: Editor: The city' s previous recycling program, which featured pickup of recyclables every other week, was too costly. The city claims that its new program, which features weekly pickup, will be more cost effective, since the greater the volume of recyclables collected per year, the more revenue the city gains from selling the recyclables. But this is absurd. People will put out the same volume of recyclables overall; it will just be spread out over a greater number of pickups.
instructions: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the editor's argument?
options: Even if the volume of collected recyclables increases, that increase might not be enough to make the recycling program cost effective.
Because of the increase in the number of pickups under the new program, the amount charged by the contractor that collects the city's recyclables will increase significantly.
The cost of collecting and disposing of general trash has been less than the cost of collecting and disposing of recyclables, and this is still likely to be the case under the new recycling program.
A weekly schedule for recyclables pickup is substantially easier for people to follow and adhere to than is a schedule of pickups every other week.
gold: A weekly schedule for recyclables pickup is substantially easier for people to follow and adhere to than is a schedule of pickups every other week.

state: Possession modification is a means of delivery of goods. In the transfer of movable property rights, both parties agreed by the assignor to continue to occupy the movable property. The right in rem becomes effective when the agreement comes into force.

A lent his necklace to B. B liked the necklace so much that he paid a certain sum of money to buy it.
A sells his house to B, but the parties agree that until A gets a new house, A will live in the house.
gold: A will sell his bicycle to B, at the same time the two sides agreed before a abroad the car is still used by A.

state: If you tell the truth in your speech, the rich will oppose you. If you lie in your speech, the poor will oppose you. When you speak, you either tell the truth or lie. So, either the rich will oppose you, or the poor will oppose you.
instructions: Which of the followings is most similar to the structure of the above reasoning??
options: If there is life on the moon, there must be air. If there is life on the moon, there must be water. There is either no air or no water on the moon. Therefore, there is no life on the moon

If the object is pressurized, its volume will become smaller. If the object is cooled, its volume will become smaller. Either pressurize the object or cool the object. Therefore, the volume of the object will become smaller

If you stimulate the tiger, the tiger will eat people. If you do not stimulate the tiger, the tiger will also eat people. Either stimulate the tiger, or do not stimulate the tiger. In short, the tiger will eat people

state: Four people are talking about Lao Tian's deposit. A said, Lao Tian has a deposit of at least 5,000 yuan. B said, No, there is at least ten thousand yuan. Lao Tian's deposit is between 5,000 yuan and 20,000 yuan
gold: Lao Tian's deposit is less than 100 yuan

state: Reduction refers to the reduction of resource consumption and waste generation in the process of production, circulation and consumption. It is a kind of circular economy.
instructions: According to the above definition, which of the following does not belong to reduction?

According to the spirit advocated by the municipal government, an enterprise eliminated its energy consuming production technology.
An agricultural production base makes comprehensive utilization of crop straw, livestock manure and waste agricultural film.
A company strictly implements product packaging standards to prevent excessive packaging.
gold: An agricultural production base makes comprehensive utilization of crop straw, livestock manure and waste agricultural film.

state: Public health experts have waged a long-standing educational campaign to get people to eat more vegetables, which are known to help prevent cancer. Unfortunately, the campaign has had little impact on people' s diets. The reason is probably that many people simply dislike the taste of most vegetables. Thus, the campaign would probably be more effective if it included information on ways to make vegetables more appetizing.
instructions: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?
options: The campaign to get people to eat more vegetables has had little impact on the diets of most people who love the taste of vegetables.
People who dislike the taste of most vegetables would eat many more vegetables if they knew how to make them more appetizing.
People who find a few vegetables appetizing typically do not eat substantially more vegetables than do people who dislike the taste of most vegetables.
Some ways of making vegetables more appetizing diminish vegetables' ability to help prevent cancer.
gold: People who dislike the taste of most vegetables would eat many more vegetables if they knew how to make them more appetizing.

state: Although withholding information from someone who would find that information painful is sometimes justified, there is no such justification if the person would benefit from having the information. Ttherefore, even though it would be painful for Jason to learn that his supervisor is displeased with his work, his colleague Jane should nonetheless inform Jason of this fact, for knowing that his supervisor was displeased would enable Jason to improve his supervisor' s opinion of his work.
instructions: Which one of the following is an assumption on which the argument relies?
options: Jason might eventually improve his supervisor's opinion of his work even if he never learns that his supervisor is displeased with his work.
If Jane tells Jason that his supervisor is displeased with his work, Jason will be grateful for the information even though it will be painful for him to learn it.
If Jane does not tell Jason that his supervisor is displeased with his work, then Jason's situation will worsen.
Jason would benefit if he were able to improve his supervisor's opinion of his work.
gold: Jason would benefit if he were able to improve his supervisor's opinion of his work.

state: Low-carbon life means that the energy consumed in daily life should be reduced as much as possible, so as to reduce carbon emissions, especially carbon dioxide emissions, so as to reduce atmospheric pollution and slow down ecological deterioration.
instructions: According to the above definition, which of the followings does not belong to the category of low-carbon life?

When using the computer, try to use low brightness, open fewer programs, and turn off the computer power during lunch break and after work
Choose to dry clothes and avoid using drum dryers
Replace jogging in the park with exercise on the treadmill
gold: Replace jogging in the park with exercise on the treadmill

state: Bethany: Psychologists have discovered a technique for replacing one' s nightmares with pleasant dreams, and have successfully taught it to adults suffering from chronic nightmares. Studies have found that nightmare-prone children are especially likely to suffer from nightmares as adults. Thus, psychologists should direct efforts toward identifying nightmare-prone children so that these children can be taught the technique for replacing their nightmares with pleasant dreams.
instructions: Which one of the following principles, if valid, most helps to justify drawing the conclusion in Bethany's argument?
options: Any psychological technique that can be successfully taught to a child can also be successfully taught to an adult.
Psychologists should do everything they can to minimize the number of adults troubled by chronic nightmares.
Psychologists should not teach the technique for replacing nightmares with pleasant dreams to children who are unlikely to suffer from nightmares as adults.
Identifying nightmare-prone children is generally more difficult than teaching adults the technique for replacing nightmares with pleasant dreams.
gold: Psychologists should do everything they can to minimize the number of adults troubled by chronic nightmares.

state: At present, although the floating population enters the city to work and live, it is not really integrated into the urban society. The isolation of the system objectively strengthens the geographical, local and kinship relationship of the population, aggravates the social differentiation, and a new dual structure appears in the city. In some cities, the floating population is upside down from the registered population, and there is a conflict of economic interest between the migrant population and the local population, which is easy to stimulate social contradictions. The family members of the floating population have been separated for a long time, resulting in irresponsible guardianship of children, lack of emotion, unstable marriage, left-behind elderly people and women, and other problems, affecting family happiness and long-term social stability.
instructions: Which of the following options is intended to be described in the above paragraph?
options: The isolation of the system makes it impossible for the floating population to integrate into the urban society.
The entry of floating population will lead to a dual structure within the city.
Only when the floating population is truly integrated into the city can the society enjoy long-term peace and stability.
Solving the problem of separation of family members of floating population is the key to disintegrating the urban dual structure.
gold: Only when the floating population is truly integrated into the city can the society enjoy long-term peace and stability.

state: Politician: fewer people are entering the labor market now than before. If the economy grows, the demand for the dynamic and educated will greatly outstrip its supply. Some companies have begun to respond to this labor market situation, looking for ways to retain existing employees. They focus on clear indicators of economic growth.

The fact that some companies are now working harder to retain their employees does not mean that they used to be indifferent to employee morale
The fact that demand will exceed supply does not mean that there is no supply at all

gold: The fact that the company is carefully preparing for possible future development does not mean that this development has taken place

state: Paleontologists can rediscover the forgotten wisdom of our ancestors. For example, the nabatas occupied the dangerous Negev desert two thousand years ago. They diverted the rainwater of the rare heavy rain in this area into irrigation ditches and reservoirs. This method was used to rebuild the ancient farms in this area, which can now produce high grain production.

options: The nabatas occupy the treacherous Negev desert.
The nabatas built irrigation ditches and reservoirs.
The nabatas irrigate with heavy rain.
Rebuild the ancient farms in this area.
gold: The nabatas built irrigation ditches and reservoirs.

state: Analyst: A recent survey showed that although professors of biology who teach but do not pursue research made up one twentieth of all science professors, they were appointed to fewer than one twentieth of all the scientific administrative positions in universities. Biology professors get more than one twentieth of all the science grant money available.

state: A music producer is recording seven records one after another: F, G, H, J, K, L and M, but it doesn't have to be in this order. state: The combat effectiveness of an army depends on the armamentthe and quality of the personnel.Georgia, which suffered heavy losses in the 2008 conflict with Russian troops, is prepared to spend 9 billion dollars to rearm its troops with modern equipment. state: We can compare life to a circle in a geometric figure. On a circle that has been drawn, it is of course very difficult to find the starting point and the ending point. The larger the radius of your life, the larger the space of your life.
instructions: Which of the followings can be inferred?
options: To measure life, you should first measure the radius of your life, including what you think, say and do.
Although life is a sacred thing full of variables, it can also be measured.
It does not mean that a man has value if he has life, and it also does not mean that he has value if he lives longer.
It is not uncommon that the value of the middle-aged is far better than that of the elderly.
gold: Although life is a sacred thing full of variables, it can also be measured.

state: A British study found that chewing can activate an immune cell called Th17 in the mouth, which can resist common bacterial and fungal infections in the mouth. Immune cells in the mouth that can resist bacterial and fungal infections can only be activated by chewing behavior.

state: The following is an excerpt from a campaign speech. state: Company Spokesperson: This year, more than 70% of the guests who stayed with us over the past summer are planning to return to our resorts for a summer vacation. state: In 2005, when the salvage company investigated the sunken ship in the sea area of Nanchuan Island, it accidentally found an ancient sunken ship containing Chinese porcelain, which was located on the sedimentary layer of the seabed. state: In a democratic society, evil is exposed to the maximum extent and condemned by public opinion, thus suppressing many evils. In anti-democratic society, evil is covered up to the maximum, which often leads to greater evil.

state: According to four major studies conducted over the past decade, the number of obese children in Beijing's urban areas has been on the rise, with more than 85 percent of children of the same age being considered obese.

state: Domesticated animals, such as dogs, have come into existence by the breeding of only the individuals of a wild species that are sufficiently tame. options: presumes without justification that college professors generally were raised in households with incomes that are average or above average for their communities
fails to note there are some communities with high average household incomes in which no college professors grew up
fails to take into account the fact that many college professors live in rural communities, which generally have low average household incomes
does not take into account the fact that college professors generally have lower salaries than their counterparts in the private sector
gold: presumes without justification that college professors generally were raised in households with incomes that are average or above average for their communities

state: Ding kiln is one of the five famous kilns in Song Dynasty, which is as famous as Ru, Guan, GE and Jun kilns. The kiln is located in Quyang, Hebei Province. Quyang County belonged to Dingzhou in the Song Dynasty, so it was named Ding kiln. Under the influence of Xing kiln, Ding kiln mainly produces white porcelain, but also burns black glaze and green glaze at the same time. The enamel of white porcelain is clear and moist, the color is mild, just like tooth carving, and the recessive is quite good. The decoration is well-known in ancient and modern times for its vivid and powerful carved and printed white porcelain, which is better than Xing kiln. The beautiful and elegant carved white porcelain and magnificent printed white porcelain in the Song and Jin dynasties are the two main varieties of Ding Kiln, representing the typical artistic style of Ding Kiln in its heyday.
instructions: Which of the followings does not match the original text?
options: The Song Dynasty and Jin Dynasty were the heyday of Ding Kiln.
Engraved and printed white porcelain is the representative work of Ding kiln.
The white porcelain of Ding kiln draws lessons from Xing kiln and exceeds that of Xing kiln.
Beauty, simplicity and elegance are a typical artistic style of Ding kiln.
gold: Beauty, simplicity and elegance are a typical artistic style of Ding kiln.

state: Fictitious consanguinity refers to the fact that the parties are not related by blood, and they are confirmed as relatives through legal procedures. In my country, fictitious consanguinity only refers to the circumstances specified in the Marriage Law and the Adoption Law.

state: A computer with signature recognition software installed - this software is limited to those who sign in the document to enter the computer - recognizes someone's signature not only by analyzing the shape of the signature, but also by analyzing features such as the pressure of the pen tip and the speed of the signature. This signature recognition software is of great value and is only used by a small number of important departments.
No one can enter the computer where the software is installed only through the skill of forging signatures.
This signature recognition software still has many defects.

state: A person who is good at thinking, thinks with his heart and has a strong desire for innovation is a fengshui place where he produces sparks and inspiration for innovation.In a sense, both creative innovation and creation always belong to those who think attentively and actively.As a front line of teaching, the classroom is also a place of innovation that can not be ignored, there are many knowledge and academic problems, waiting for people to study here should become an inexhaustible source of scientific and technological innovation.

state: Liang: Watching movies in which violence is portrayed as an appropriate way to resolve problems increases levels of aggression in viewers. instructions: The dialogue provides the most support for inferring that Liang and Sarah agree with each other that
options: if violence in certain movies causes violence in viewers, access to those movies should be restricted
people who experience an emotion vicariously are likely to purge themselves of that emotion
the members of a mature audience are unlikely to believe that violence is sometimes an appropriate way to resolve problems
the effects of dramatic depictions of violence on audiences are at least partially understood
gold: the effects of dramatic depictions of violence on audiences are at least partially understood

state: A professor organized 120 young participants to familiarize them with a false city on the computer. Then let them find out the shortest route to the key landmarks at the specified location as quickly as possible and finally let them identify the scent of 40 aromatic plants, such as Zanthoxylum bungeanum and Zanthoxylum bungeanum. It was found that those who scored higher in the pathfinding task had a better sense of smell. The professor infers that a person's good spatial memory and strong sense of direction will make his sense of smell more sensitive.
instructions: Which of the following, if true, can best question the professor's above conjecture?
options: Most animals mainly rely on their sense of smell to find food and avoid predators and the evolution of their sense of smell helps to navigate.
Some of the participants are gourmets who are often invited to enjoy delicious food in specialty restaurants throughout the city.
Some of the participants are marathon runners who often take part in marathons held by some cities.
In the same test, the professor himself was inferior to young people in terms of olfactory sensitivity and spatial orientation.
gold: In the same test, the professor himself was inferior to young people in terms of olfactory sensitivity and spatial orientation.

state: James: Chemists have recently invented a new technique for extracting rhodium, an element necessary for manufacturing catalytic converters for automobiles, from nuclear waste. indicating that James is assuming the truth of the conclusion that he intends to establish
casting doubt on the accuracy of the claims made by James in support of his conclusion
questioning the credibility of advocates of nuclear power

state: A chemical plant produces an insecticide that makes small mammals such as otters infertile. After the factory began operation, the incidence of infertility of an otter living in a nearby river increased rapidly. Therefore, the factory must have polluted the river when producing pesticides.

gold: A low-calcium diet can lead to a decline in poultry egg production. When chickens on a farm are released to look for food in the spring, their egg production is significantly reduced. Therefore, the food they find and eat must be very low in calcium

state: Editorial: The town would not need to spend as much as it does on removing trash if all town residents sorted their household garbage. However, while telling residents that they must sort their garbage would get some of them to do so, many would resent the order and refuse to comply. The current voluntary system, then, is to be preferred, because it costs about as much as a nonvoluntary system would and it does not engender nearly as much resentment.
instructions: The contention that the town would not have to spend as much as it does on removing trash if all town residents sorted their garbage plays which one of the following roles in the editorial's argument?
options: It is a claim that the editorial is trying to show is false.
It is a fact granted by the editorial that lends some support to an alternative to the practice that the editorial defends as preferable.
It is an example of a difficulty facing the claim that the editorial is attempting to refute.
It is a premise that the editorial's argument relies on in reaching its conclusion.
gold: It is a fact granted by the editorial that lends some support to an alternative to the practice that the editorial defends as preferable.

state: With the improvement of social civilization, women's talents have not only gained more display space in highly rational industries such as media, universities, scientific research and finance, but also helped them to create more and more remarkable achievements. Women are more suitable for highly rational professions such as media, universities, scientific research and finance
With the improvement of professionalization, women need to pay more to succeed in their careers

state: Most plants produce chemicals that resist parasites in the process of long-term evolution. Plants commonly used by humans contain about 40 natural drugs, that is, complex chemical toxins against bacteria, fungi and other parasites. People ingest these toxins every day without poisoning, so the new harm caused by synthetic pesticides sprayed on crops is very small.
instructions: If the following statement is true, which of the followings does not undermine the above argument?
options: The concentration of natural drugs in plants is much lower than that of synthetic pesticides sprayed on crops
Humans have been ingesting the natural drugs contained in these plants for thousands of years and have time to adapt to them
The chemical structure of synthetic pesticides is usually simpler than that of natural drugs contained in plants
Natural drugs contained in plants are usually only suitable for resisting specific organisms, while synthetic pesticides are usually harmful to a variety of organisms
gold: The chemical structure of synthetic pesticides is usually simpler than that of natural drugs contained in plants

state: A certain gene can be stimulated by chemicals in cigarette smoke, causing lung cells to metabolize the chemicals in a way that makes the cells cancerous. Yet smokers in whom this gene is not stimulated have as high a risk of developing lung cancer from smoking as other smokers do.
instructions: If the statements above are true, it can be concluded on the basis of them that
options: the gene is more likely to be stimulated by chemicals in cigarette smoke than by other chemicals
stimulation of the gene by chemicals in cigarette smoke is not the only factor affecting the risk for smokers of developing lung cancer
nonsmokers have as high a risk of developing lung cancer as do smokers in whom the gene has not been stimulated
smokers are less likely to develop lung cancer if they do not have the gene
gold: stimulation of the gene by chemicals in cigarette smoke is not the only factor affecting the risk for smokers of developing lung cancer

state: The traditional view of the Roman emperor Caligula as a cruel and insane tyrant has been challenged by some modern historians. They point out that little documentation of Caligula' s alleged cruelty or outrageous behavior survives from the time of his reign and that the histories that have come down to us were written by his enemies.
instructions: Which one of the following, if true, adds the most support for the challenge from the modem historians?
options: People who have lived under someone regarded as a cruel tyrant are more likely to view that person unfavorably than favorably.
The specific outrageous acts attributed to Caligula in Roman documentation are very similar to acts attributed in earlier writings to other rulers alleged to be cruel tyrants.
There is less documentation of any sort from Caligula's reign than from the reigns of most other Roman emperors of Caligula's era.
There is ample documentation of modern tyrants being responsible for outrageous acts worse than those attributed to Caligula.
gold: The specific outrageous acts attributed to Caligula in Roman documentation are very similar to acts attributed in earlier writings to other rulers alleged to be cruel tyrants.

state: Some theorists argue that literary critics should strive to be value-neutral in their literary criticism. These theorists maintain that by exposing the meaning of literary works without evaluating them, critics will enable readers to make their own judgments about the works' merits. But literary criticism cannot be completely value-neutral. Thus, some theorists are mistaken about what is an appropriate goal for literary criticism.
instructions: The argument's conclusion follows logically if which one of the following is assumed?
options: Any critic who is able to help readers make their own judgments about literary works' merits should strive to produce value-neutral criticism.
If it is impossible to produce completely value- neutral literary criticism, then critics should not even try to be value-neutral.
The less readers understand the meaning of a literary work, the less capable they will be of evaluating that work's merits.
Critics are more likely to provide criticisms of the works they like than to provide criticisms of the works they dislike.
gold: If it is impossible to produce completely value- neutral literary criticism, then critics should not even try to be value-neutral.

state: During the summer vacation, Xiao Zhang's parents reported to Xiao Zhang a photography interest class and an art interest class. After knowing this, Xiao Zhang said, I don't want to be a photographer in the future. There's no need to learn photography.

Xiao Zhang wants to be a painter rather than a photographer.
Only if you want to be a photographer, you need to learn photography.
Xiao Zhang prefers painting to photography.
gold: Only if you want to be a photographer, you need to learn photography.

state: Mariah: Joanna has argued that Adam should not judge the essay contest because several of his classmates have entered the contest. However, the essays are not identified by author to the judge and, moreover, none of Adam' s friends are classmates of his. Still, Adam has no experience in critiquing essays. instructions: Which one of the following principles, if valid, most helps to justify Mariah's argument?
options: A suspicion of bias is insufficient grounds on which to disqualify someone from judging a contest.
In selecting a contest judge, fairness concerns should override concern for the appropriate expertise.
Expertise should be the primary prerequisite for serving as a contest judge.

state: Skim pricing strategy refers to a pricing strategy in which manufacturers take advantage of consumers' psychology of novelty and novelty, seize the favorable opportunity when competitors have not appeared or the competition is not fierce, and set the product price very high, so as to obtain as much profit as possible in the short term and recover the investment as soon as possible.
instructions: According to the above definition, which of the following behaviors belongs to skim pricing strategy:
options: A star hotel renovated and raised the standard room price by 200 yuan
Due to the rise in the price of raw materials, an automobile dealer asked the orderer to make up the car payment
A certain brand of clothing discount has been processed for seasonal clothing, but the new seasonal products are sold at a high price
A shopping mall raised the original price of goods during the festival, and then promoted them with attractive discounts
gold: A certain brand of clothing discount has been processed for seasonal clothing, but the new seasonal products are sold at a high price

state: Because the interest rate of mortgage loans is decreasing, and many consumers are waiting to see how low the interest rate will be, the number of new homes sold in January has fallen sharply. While sales have fallen sharply, the average price of new homes sold has skyrocketed.

The prices of new houses have been rising slowly over the past three years as the severity of the housing shortage has increased
More homeowners sold their mid-priced homes again in January than in the previous three months
gold: Sales of higher-priced houses were not affected by the decline in sales, as their buyers were less constrained by the total payment

state: Is the decline in economic growth due to an ageing population? The conclusion is that the younger the population, the poorer the country, and vice versa. So why the fear of ageing? In most countries around the world, young people are better educated than their elders, and a smaller population might be compensated for by raising their productivity levels through higher education.
instructions: Which of the following is the text intended to illustrate?
options: People are perfectly capable of dealing with an ageing population
We should analyze the impact of population aging on economy from multiple angles
An aging population has no impact on economic growth
An aging population has a negative impact on economic growth
gold: We should analyze the impact of population aging on economy from multiple angles

state: Researchers have cultivated certain fry in normal seawater and seawater containing twice the concentration of carbon dioxide. The fry grows up and are placed in a maze. Whenever they encounter obstacles, fish hatched in normal seawater will choose the right direction to avoid the obstacles. However, the fish that hatched under high carbon dioxide concentration will randomly choose to turn left or right, so that this fish has a reduced chance of survival when encountering natural enemies. Therefore, the researchers believe that the ability of fish to survive in a high carbon dioxide environment will be weakened.
instructions: Which of the followings, if true, does not support the conclusion?
options: About one-third of the carbon dioxide produced by humans burning fossil fuels is absorbed by the oceans on the earth, which makes the sea water gradually acidic, which will soften the shells and bones of marine organisms.

In marine areas with high carbon dioxide concentration, the oxygen concentration is low. Less oxygen makes it difficult for marine life to breathe, and it becomes more difficult for foraging, avoiding predators and reproducing offspring.

Carbon dioxide is an important nutrient for many marine plants. They convert the carbon dioxide absorbed by the leaves and the water transported by the roots into sugar, starch and oxygen under sunlight.
The juvenile clownfish were raised in seawater with a high carbon dioxide concentration and played the sounds of natural enemies. As a result, this group of small fish could not hear the sound.
gold: Carbon dioxide is an important nutrient for many marine plants. They convert the carbon dioxide absorbed by the leaves and the water transported by the roots into sugar, starch and oxygen under sunlight.

state: At the last meeting of the school-level professional title evaluation committee, member Professor Zhang believed that this committee was the least influential in recent years. state: Several recent studies establish that most people would want to be informed if they had any serious medical condition. In each study, over 80 percent of the people surveyed indicated that they would want to be told.

state: Alternative causality means that two or more actors have committed dangerous acts that may cause damage to others and have caused damage results, but it is impossible to determine who is the perpetrator.

gold: A, B and C went out hunting with the same shotgun and bullets. A and B saw a prey near C. they fired at the same time, and one of them hit C.

state: Artistic intuition is that people directly feel and comprehend the characteristics, essence, and meaning of things in artistic activities without logical reasoning and analysis.

state: To prevent a newly built dam on the Chiff River from blocking the route of fish migrating to breeding grounds upstream, the dam includes a fish pass, a mechanism designed to allow fish through the dam. state: In 1990, the incidence of bone fractures  was very high among people over 70 years old in W city, and at the same time, the mortality rate of people over 70 years old was also very high, so it can be known that the high incidence of bone fractures  led to an increase in mortality among people over 70 years old.

state: The American Ornithology Foundation recently released a report on the state of birds in the United States. state: With the strengthening of the judicial principle of who claims, who gives evidence, whether strong evidence can be collected has become the key to the success or failure of civil litigation. state: What is our purpose of helping poor students? They want to have equal access to education and not lose their natural right to grow up happily because of some social disasters. state: If the regulation of computer networks is to be modeled on past legislation, then its model must be either legislation regulating a telephone system or else legislation regulating a public broadcasting service. If the telephone model is used, computer networks will be held responsible only for ensuring that messages get transmitted. If the public broadcast model is used, computer networks will additionally be responsible for the content of those messages. Yet a computer network serves both these sorts of functions: it can serve as a private message service or as a publicly accessible information service. Thus neither of these models can be appropriate for computer networks.
instructions: The passage is structured to lead to which one of the following conclusions?

Legislators who do not have extensive experience with computers should not attempt to write legislation regulating computer networks.
The regulation of computer networks should not be modeled on any single piece of past legislation.
A computer network merely duplicates the functions of a telephone system and a television network.
gold: The regulation of computer networks should not be modeled on any single piece of past legislation.

state: People who are in favor of the death penalty usually give two reasons: first, the fear of death will prevent others from committing the same terrible crime; second, the death penalty is cheaper than its alternative, life imprisonment. However, reliable research shows that life imprisonment is preferable to the death penalty from an economic point of view. People think that it is not true that the death penalty saves money. Therefore, the death penalty should be abolished.
instructions: Logically, which of the followings is an appropriate evaluation of the argument in the main part of the question?
options: The structure of the argument is acceptable, because human life is more precious than anything else
The argument has logical power because its reason is true and human life is at stake
The argument does not take into account another important reason in favor of the death penalty, so it is not a good argument
It is only natural to abolish the death penalty and there is no need to discuss it
gold: The argument does not take into account another important reason in favor of the death penalty, so it is not a good argument

state: It is generally believed that occurrence of tumors is the result of mutations in related genes of multiple tumors, that is, the accumulation of mutations in related genes of multiple tumors leads to uncontrolled cell division and proliferation, and finally becomes tumor cells. However, a single gene mutation is not enough to cause tumor, because cells have mechanisms such as DNA damage repair and replication error correction, which can effectively repair gene mutations and prevent mutated cells from continuing to divide. However, if the cells containing related gene mutations escape DNA damage repair and replication correction and continue to divide and proliferate, they have more chances to accumulate more mutations, thus defecting into tumor cells.
instructions: Which of the following options is intended to be emphasized in this passage?
options: The development of tumor cells is restricted by many factors.
Normal cells can be transformed into tumor cells under certain conditions.
The formation of tumor cells is directly related to the number of gene mutations.
There are limitations in the mechanisms of DNA damage repair and replication error correction in cells.
gold: The formation of tumor cells is directly related to the number of gene mutations.

state: In the first decade following the founding of the British Labour party, the number of people regularly voting for Labour increased fivefold. The number of committed Labour voters increased a further fivefold during the party' s second decade. Since the increase was thus the same in the first as in the second decade, the often-made claim that the Labour party gained more voters in the party' s second decade than in its first is clearly false.
instructions: The reasoning in the argument is flawed because the argument

fails to allow for the possibility that the policy positions advocated by the Labour party changed during the period in question
fails to specify dates necessary to evaluate the truth of the conclusion, even though the argument depends on distinguishing between two time periods
draws a conclusion that cannot be true if all the data advanced in its support are true
gold: draws a conclusion that cannot be true if all the data advanced in its support are true

state: In order to protect the legal rights and interests of migrant workers, the labor department of A place tailor-made a migrant worker rights protection card for migrant workers, which compiled and printed the rights and obligations of workers, labor dispute resolution steps, and consultation telephone numbers on the card. ,It is issued to migrant workers during the Spring Festival. state: Distributed energy system refers to a variety of modular power generation devices that are integrated or used alone, close to small users and have a capacity range of thousands of watts to 50 megawatts. state: As part of a survey, approximately 10, 000 randomly selected individuals were telephoned and asked a number of questions about their income and savings. state: Self-control is not only about control oneself, but also includes the ability to eliminate interference from irrelevant stimuli and persist in completing related tasks (even tasks that one does not like). There are different views from various schools in academic circles on whether self-control is stable  and unchangeable  or can be consumed. Psychologists divided the experimental subjects into two groups and asked them to solve problems in the same field. One group could only eat radishes when solving problems, and the other group could also eat biscuits. As a result, the group that only ate radishes gave up earlier because they not only resisted the temptation of biscuits but also consumed self-control. From this, psychologists conclude that people's self-control is limited, and overuse of it will lead to a decrease.
instructions: Which of the followings should be added as a prerequisite for the rationality of the above conclusion?
options: The subjects' interest in solving problems is not exactly the same.
Biscuits and radishes have different allures to test subjects.
Biscuits and radishes have different effects in replenishing human body's energy.
The anti-interference ability of the two groups of subjects is not exactly the same.
gold: Biscuits and radishes have different allures to test subjects.

state: It is now a common complaint that the electronic media have corroded the intellectual skills required and fostered by the literary media. state: Newspaper editors should not allow reporters to write the headlines for their own stories. state: Landing on Mars is not an easy task. When the Earth and Mars are closest, there is also a distance of 56 million kilometers, which is 140 times the distance between the Earth and the moon. state: The Gulches is an area of volcanic rock that is gashed by many channels that lead downhill from the site of a prehistoric glacier to a river. The channels clearly were cut by running water. state: When Copernicus changed the way we think about the solar system, he did so not by discovering new information, but by looking differently at information already available. state: To the Editor: In 1960, an astronomer proposed a mathematical model for determining whether extraterrestrial life exists. state: On the nights immediately following the mysterious Tunguska event, which destroyed a tract of Siberian wilderness in 1908, eyewitnesses reported seeing noctilucent clouds -- brilliant night-visible clouds made up of ice particles that form rarely and only at very high altitudes. state: Ecologist: Smallpox, one of the worst diseases ever to afflict humans, has in some outbreaks killed as much as 50 percent of local populations. state: Treatment for hypertension forestalls certain medical expenses by preventing strokes and heart disease. state: Economist: Some policymakers believe that our country' s continued economic growth requires a higher level of personal savings than we currently have. A recent legislative proposal would allow individuals to set up savings accounts in which interest earned would be exempt from taxes until money is withdrawn from the account. Backers of this proposal claim that its implementation would increase the amount of money available for banks to loan at a relatively small cost to the government in lost tax revenues. Yet, when similar tax-incentive programs were tried in the past, virtually all of the money invested through them was diverted from other personal savings, and the overall level of personal savings was unchanged.
instructions: The passage as a whole provides the most support for which one of the following conclusions?
options: The proposed tax incentive is unlikely to attract enough additional money into personal savings accounts to make up for the attendant loss in tax revenues.
Backers of the tax-incentive proposal undoubtedly have some motive other than their expressed aim of increasing the amount of money available for banks to loan.
The economy will be in danger unless some alternative to increased personal savings can be found to stimulate growth.
A tax-incentive program that resulted in substantial loss of tax revenues would be likely to generate a large increase in personal savings.
gold: The proposed tax incentive is unlikely to attract enough additional money into personal savings accounts to make up for the attendant loss in tax revenues.

state: A scientist made three observations: (1) in the world' s temperate zones, food is more plentiful in the ocean than it is in fresh water; (2) migratory fish in temperate zones generally mature in the ocean and spawn in fresh water; and (3) migratory fish need much nourishment as they mature but little or none during the part of their lives when they spawn. whether in the world's temperate zones, the temperatures of bodies of fresh water tend to be lower than those of the regions of the oceans into which they flow

gold: whether in the tropics food is less plentiful in the ocean than in fresh water

state: Classical Roman architecture is beautiful, primarily because of its use of rounded arches and its symmetry. state: In 1616, Shakespeare and Tang Xianzu died in the same year. Both of them can be regarded as great playwrights at the turn of the 16th and 17th centuries. They both love to write plays, but their writing methods are different. For example, as the story of Romeo and Juliet draws to a close, a pair of lovers died in love, and the tragic tragedy ends with reconciliation between the two families. The willingness to reconcile is indeed wonderful, but unfortunately, Shakespeare's writing used for reconciliation are too casual, as if it was just for the concept of reconciliation. Du Liniang in the Peony Pavilion thought, mourned and died because of the encounter in her dream, and then survived and became satisfied. Tang Xianzu sprinkled his pen and ink on love without wasting on hate, deliberated on tenderness without indulging in violence. state: Optical tweezers is a technology that uses a three-dimensional potential well formed by a highly convergent laser beam to capture, manipulate and control tiny particles. state: Sonic boom is that when the aircraft breaks through the sound barrier, due to the compression of the air can not spread rapidly, it will gradually form a shock surface. The highly concentrated acoustic energy on the shock surface causes a loud sound, which makes people feel a short and extremely strong explosion. Sonic boom occur only when they break through the sound barrier, that is, flying at supersonic speeds. The sonic booms cloud is a conical cloud with the aircraft as the central axis and spreads uniformly from the front of the wing to all sides. It is mainly due to the fact that the velocity of the air flow is faster than the conduction speed of the air when breaking through the speed of sound, which can not effectively pull down the airflow, resulting in a decrease in density, a decrease in air pressure, and water vapor condensing into tiny water droplets, which looks like a cloud-like state to the naked eye. Sonic boom cloud often appear in transonic flights, but not only in transonic flights.
instructions: According to the above definition, which of the following options is correct?

The appearance of sonic boom cloud marks the generation of sonic boom.
The appearance of the sonic boom cloud indicates that the sound barrier has been broken
Supersonic flight when sonic boom occurs
gold: Supersonic flight when sonic boom occurs

state: Film historians have made two major criticisms of Depression-era filmmakers: first, that they were too uncritical of the economic status quo; and second, that they self-indulgently created films reflecting their own dreams and desires. state: The hot stove effect means that anyone in the organization who violates the rules and regulations will be punished. In many fundamental ways, what was considered beautiful in those cultures is still considered beautiful in our own time.
instructions: Which one of the following statements, if true, most weakens the argument?

Our own standard of beauty was strongly influenced by our exposure to works that were considered beautiful in earlier cultures.
Few contemporary artists have been significantly exposed to the art of earlier cultures.
The arts held a much more important place in earlier cultures than they do in our culture.
gold: Our own standard of beauty was strongly influenced by our exposure to works that were considered beautiful in earlier cultures.

state: At present, China's socialist democracy and legal system is still in the stage of gradual improvement. The phenomenon of non-compliance with the law and lax law enforcement still exist to varying degrees. Paying taxes according to the law and conscientiously has not yet become a tight string in the mind of every citizen, especially since the introduction of the individual income tax, the state of collection and payment has always been unsatisfactory.
instructions: Which of the following can be inferred?
options: We need to strengthen citizens' awareness of paying taxes.
Citizens who do not pay personal income tax are subject to arrest.
Citizens who do not pay personal income tax shall be severely punished.
All citizens should be subject to individual income tax.
gold: We need to strengthen citizens' awareness of paying taxes.

state: In foreign countries, many genetic and infectious diseases belong to the category of citizens' privacy. In our country, it is quite common for some institutions to disclose these privacy of citizens at will. The law still lacks relevant regulations and effective protections, resulting in the disclosure of such privacy. Unable to obtain judicial relief.
instructions: Through this passage, which of the following does the author want to express?
options: Relevant institutions in our country should strictly protect the privacy of citizens' illnesses
The personal privacy protection awareness of Chinese citizens is still relatively weak
my country's legal system for protecting personal privacy needs to be improved urgently
In terms of medical care, there is still a certain gap between our country and other countries
gold: my country's legal system for protecting personal privacy needs to be improved urgently

state: Essayist: Wisdom and intelligence are desirable qualities. However, being wise does not mean that he is wise, and being wise does not mean that he is wise. Some of the people I've met are intelligent and some are wise, but no one has both qualities at the same time.
instructions: Which of the followings cannot be true if the essayist's statement is valid?
options: No one is intelligent but not wise, and no one is wise but not intelligent.
Most people are both intelligent and wise.
No one is both intelligent and wise.
Most people are neither intelligent nor wise.
gold: No one is intelligent but not wise, and no one is wise but not intelligent.

state: One eighth of the eight planets in the solar system where the earth is located have life. In this proportion, considering the existence of a huge number of planets in the universe. Therefore, the number of living celestial bodies in the universe must be extremely huge.
instructions: The flaw in the above argument is that it presupposes without proof:
options: If a celestial body is similar to the earth, there must be life.
If a galaxy is similar to the solar system, it must have exactly eight planets.
The planets of the solar system are similar to many planets in the universe.
Similar to life on earth, it can live on other planets with different conditions.
gold: The planets of the solar system are similar to many planets in the universe.

state: The inclusion of traditional festivals into national legal festivals reflects the respect for Chinese traditional culture and the return of Chinese traditional culture is an important part of our spiritual home, but in recent years, more and more foreign festivals have become fashionable traditional festivals, but they are regarded as faded by people, especially young people.
instructions: Which of the following does not fit the meaning of the passage?
options: The author supports the practice of bringing traditional festivals into national statutory programs
Traditional festivals are an important part of Chinese traditional culture
Some foreign festivals are becoming more and more fashionable, and most young people have forgotten the traditional festivals
Bringing traditional festivals into national legal festivals can arouse everyone's attention to traditional culture
gold: Some foreign festivals are becoming more and more fashionable, and most young people have forgotten the traditional festivals

state: The development and progress of human medicine not only benefit from the hard work of scientists, but also from the silent sacrifice of experimental animals. Before drug development into the clinical, we need to do a lot of animal experiments to explore the efficacy, toxicity, safe dose of drugs. However, there are many differences between human beings and rats, pigs, dogs, rabbits and other animals after all. Even if we have a correct understanding of the physiological structure of animals and the law of drug reaction, we can not easily and blindly transfer the result of our understanding to human beings.
instructions: Which of the following, if true, best supports this view?
options: According to the results of his anatomy of animals, Galen, an ancient Greek medical scientist, believed that whether in human veins or arteries, blood is an one-way movement, not a circular movement. Of course, this is not in line with the concept of modern science.

In the Song Dynasty, Materia Medica Yan Yi recorded that some wild geese with broken wings were fed with natural copper, and then the wild geese flew away. In the eyes of modern people, it is unthinkable to eat natural copper to treat fractures.

In 1882, German Robert Koch used guinea pigs to do experiments and concluded that tuberculosis is the causative bacterium of tuberculosis. Whether it comes from monkeys, cattle or humans, it has the same symptoms. For this discovery, he won the Nobel Prize.

In 1957, a pregnancy response drug called thalidomide was put on the market after being tested on rats. After a period of time, it was discovered that thalidomide can cause malformations in human fetuses, but it will not cause teratogenicity to rat fetuses.
gold: In 1957, a pregnancy response drug called thalidomide was put on the market after being tested on rats. After a period of time, it was discovered that thalidomide can cause malformations in human fetuses, but it will not cause teratogenicity to rat fetuses.

state: Xiao Li made an appointment with his friend: if it's sunny tomorrow, I'll go hiking with you.
instructions: According to this, which of the following can be deduced when Xiao Li breaks his appointment?
options: The sun will be shining tomorrow, Xiao Li did go outing with friends
It will be sunny tomorrow, but Xiao Li didn't go hiking with his friends.
It rains tomorrow, Xiao Li is still going out with friends
It's raining tomorrow, Xiao Li didn't go outing with friends
gold: It will be sunny tomorrow, but Xiao Li didn't go hiking with his friends.

state: Principle: Meetings should be kept short, addressing only those issues relevant to a majority of those attending. A person should not be required to attend a meeting if none of the issues to be addressed at the meeting are relevant to that person. Application: Terry should not be required to attend today' s two o' clock meeting.
instructions: Which one of the following, if true, most justifies the stated application of the principle?
options: No issue relevant to Terry could be relevant to a majority of those attending the meeting.
If Terry attends the meeting a different set of issues will be relevant to a majority of those attending than if Terry does not attend.
If Terry makes a presentation at the meeting, the meeting will not be kept short.
The majority of the issues to be addressed at the meeting are not relevant to Terry.
gold: No issue relevant to Terry could be relevant to a majority of those attending the meeting.

state: Unlike traditional coal, gas and atomic energy, solar energy does not produce pollution, does not need to be transported, has no risk of radiation, and is not subject to power companies. Therefore, people should be encouraged to use solar energy.
instructions: If which of the following statements is true, it will most strongly weaken the above argument?
options: Few people have studied how solar energy can be used in homes
The cost of solar energy equipment to meet the needs of a family of four is equal to the cost of traditional energy needed by the family for a year
An effective way to collect and preserve solar energy for a long time has not been found
Opponents of the use of solar energy believe that doing so will lead to an energy monopoly
gold: An effective way to collect and preserve solar energy for a long time has not been found

state: Arthur Okun, a famous American economist, found the empirical relationship between economic growth rate and unemployment rate in cyclical fluctuations, that is, when the real GDP growth decreases by 2% relative to the potential GDP growth (generally defined as 3% in the United States), the unemployment rate increases by about 1%. This rule, named after its discoverer, is called Okun's law. This concept was first proposed by Okun. It refers to the maximum output value generated by a country's economy while maintaining relatively stable prices. Potential GDP is also known as full employment GDP.
instructions: Which of the followings is the same as the above analysis method?
options: The frog's legs have a great pedaling force on the water surface, and the water has a great reaction force on the frog. People were inspired to imitate the frog and invented breaststroke.
The speed of the gear is inversely proportional to the number of teeth, that is, the more teeth of the gear, the slower the speed of the gear.

Bats can fly fast at night and avoid obstacles because their ears can hear the echo of ultrasonic waves when they encounter obstacles. If their ears were plugged, they may hit obstacles. If their eyes were covered, it may not hit obstacles.
If there is a broom cloud in the sky, it will rain heavily in three days.
gold: If there is a broom cloud in the sky, it will rain heavily in three days.

state: Ann: All the campers at Camp Winnehatchee go to Tri-Cities High School. Bill: That' s not true. Some Tri-Cities students are campers at Camp Lakemont.
instructions: Bill's answer can be best explained on the assumption that he has interpreted Ann's remark to mean that
options: some Tri-Cities High School students have withdrawn from Camp Lakemont
most of the campers at Camp Lakemont come from high schools other than Tri-Cities
only campers at Camp Winnehatchee are students at Tri-Cities High School
most Tri-Cities High School students are campers at Camp Winnehatchee
gold: only campers at Camp Winnehatchee are students at Tri-Cities High School

state: A doctor who has long studied drunkenness and alcoholism found that in general, drunken people are much more likely to be violent than non-drinkers or moderate drinkers. Accordingly, the doctor concluded that people with violent tendencies were more likely to get drunk.
instructions: Which of the following most seriously weaken the doctor's judgment?
options: Some people who have never had a drink also have a strong tendency to violence.
When people are addicted to alcohol, people tend to get out of control and behave violently.
The doctor studied not only violent tendencies, but also other bad habits.
When people are drunk, they often use violence to vent their discontent.
gold: Some people who have never had a drink also have a strong tendency to violence.

state: Zoologist: It is true that over the past 15 years, there has been a fourfold increase in government funding to preserve endangered species, while the number of endangered species needing such preservation has increased by only 70% (there were, however, a large number of endangered species to begin with 15 years ago). Taking into account inflation, the amount of funding is at least double what it was 15 years ago. Nevertheless, the current amount of funding from the government for species preservation is inadequate and must be enhanced.
instructions: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to reconcile the zoologist's conclusion with the above evidence?
options: The two government agencies responsible for species preservation are typically under budget and are known for an utter lack of cooperation.
Unlike today, funding for the preservation of species was essentially nonexistent 15 years ago.
Over the past 15 years, the salaries of conservationists employed by the government to work on species preservation solutions have increased at a rate twice that of inflation.

Within the past 15 years, there have been breakthroughs in species demography that allow scientists to identify those species most in need of protection far before they face any real risk of extinction.
gold: Unlike today, funding for the preservation of species was essentially nonexistent 15 years ago.

state: Common dangerous behavior refers to the infringement that more than two people jointly commit endangering the personal safety of others and causes damage consequences, while the actual infringement can not be determined. After the establishment of the common dangerous act, although the real perpetrator can only be one or a part of the person, but if it is not possible to determine who is the real perpetrator of the violation, the joint perpetrators of the harmful acts of several people bear joint and several responsibilities.
instructions: Which of the following options is correct, as defined above?
options: Wang was killed in a collision on a highway late one night, and it was later determined that a total of five vehicles were passing through the section, but it was not possible to determine the vehicle involved, so the five drivers acted in a common and dangerous act
The behaviour of the three men, who were drunk and threw glass bottles downstairs, one of which smashed passers-by into serious injury, constituted a common and dangerous act

Zhao put the motor vehicle downstairs in a residential area, the next morning found that the car was hit by a flowerpot falling upstairs, the vehicle was seriously damaged. Since it is not possible to determine which household the pot fell from, all occupants of the building bear joint and several responsibilities for common hazardous behaviour

Huang and other four people quarrelled over trivia, and then beat each other, onlookers had a front to persuade, pull was pushed down, had been trampled by four people injured, then Huang and other four people's behavior constitutes a common dangerous behavior
gold: The behaviour of the three men, who were drunk and threw glass bottles downstairs, one of which smashed passers-by into serious injury, constituted a common and dangerous act

state: Pain perception depends only partly on physiology. During World War II a significantly lower percentage of injured soldiers requested morphine than did civilians recuperating from surgery. The soldier' s response to injury was relief, joy at being alive, even euphoria; to the civilians, surgery was a depressing, calamitous event. So it would seem that the meaning one attaches to a wound can affect the amount of pain one perceives.
instructions: The claim that pain perception depends only partly on physiology figures in the argument in which one of the following ways?
options: It summarizes a position that the argument is meant to discredit.
It is the main conclusion of the argument.
It undermines the argument's main conclusion.
It is an assumption on which the argument depends.
gold: It is the main conclusion of the argument.

state: In ancient Greece, court witnesses were not crossexamined and the jury, selected from the citizenry, received no guidance on points of law; thus, it was extremely important for litigants to make a good impression on the jurors. For this reason, courtroom oratory by litigants is a good source of data on the common conceptions of morality held by the citizens of ancient Greece.
instructions: Which one of the following, if true, would most strengthen the argument?
options: Litigants believed jurors were likely to be impressed by litigants whose professed moral code most resembled their own.
Litigants believed jurors were likely to render their decisions based on a good understanding of the law.
Litigants believed jurors were more likely to be impressed by litigants whose personality they preferred.
Litigants believed jurors were more likely to subject the litigants' personal moral codes to close critical scrutiny than were people who did not sit on juries.
gold: Litigants believed jurors were likely to be impressed by litigants whose professed moral code most resembled their own.

state: Situation: Someone living in a cold climate buys a winter coat that is stylish but not warm in order to appear sophisticated. Analysis: People are sometimes willing to sacrifice sensual comfort or pleasure for the sake of appearances.
instructions: The analysis provided for the situation above is most appropriate for which one of the following situations?
options: A person sets her thermostat at a low temperature during the winter because she is concerned about the environmental damage caused by using fossil fuels to heat her home.
A parent buys a car seat for a young child because it is more colorful and more comfortable for the child than the other car seats on the market, though no safer.
A couple buys a particular wine even though their favorite wine is less expensive and better tasting because they think it will impress their dinner guests.
An acrobat convinces the circus that employs him to purchase an expensive outfit for him so that he can wear it during his act to impress the audience.
gold: A couple buys a particular wine even though their favorite wine is less expensive and better tasting because they think it will impress their dinner guests.

state: Music critic: Fewer and fewer musicians are studying classical music, decreasing the likelihood that those with real aptitude for such music will be performing it. Audiences who hear these performances will not appreciate classical music's greatness and will thus decamp to other genres. So to maintain classical music's current meager popularity, we must encourage more young musicians to enter the field.
instructions: Which of the following, if true, most weakens the music critic's reasoning?
options: Musicians who choose to study classical music do so because they believe they have an aptitude for the music.
It is possible to enjoy the music in a particular genre even when it is performed by musicians who are not ideally suited for that genre.
The continued popularity of a given genre of music depends in part on the audiences being able to understand why that genre attained its original popularity.
Most people who appreciate classical music come to do so through old recordings rather than live performances.
gold: Most people who appreciate classical music come to do so through old recordings rather than live performances.

state: We can be sure that at least some halogen lamps are well crafted, because halogen lamps from most major manufacturers are on display at Furniture Labyrinth. Any item on display at Furniture Labyrinth is well crafted.
instructions: Which one of the following arguments is most similar in its reasoning to the argument above?
options: We can be sure that Gianna will get at least some good mechanical work done to her car, because she can have her car worked on at any of several shops in the city, and every shop is capable of doing good mechanical work.
We can be positive that there are at least a few disturbing sonnets, given that Melinda has written several different kinds of sonnets; everything Melinda writes is disturbing.
